animate and in animate is filled with the nature of Lord Shiva, then where is Bondage? Bondage
is nowhere. For this question, to remove this question, the author puts down another sutra
by joining and separating these two sutras, that is to say by uniting the letter A and not uniting
it. Chaitanya Mahatma, Janam Bandha. First reading, when you unite letter, is Chaitanya Mahatma, Janam Bandha.
Then you unite this letter. Then the reading will be Chaitanya Mahatma and Janam Bandha. So,
he defines the meaning of Jan in two ways, Janam Bandha. Knowledge is Bondage.
Different, Shaitanya Mahatma, knowing is Bondage and not knowing, undifferentiatedly is Bondage.
So, knowing is Bondage and not knowing is Bondage. Janam is Bondha and Agjan is also Bondha.
When you know in a differentiated way, that is Bondage. When you don't know the undifferentiated way,
that is Bondage. Not knowing is Bondage, knowing is Bondage. These two meanings come out from this Janam
Bandha because first sutra was Chaitanya Mahatma and there Agjanam Bandha will come out. If you unite
this sutra with the previous one. If you don't unite this sutra with the previous one, then Janam Bandha
will come. Knowledge is Bondage. Which knowledge is Bondage? Differentiated knowledge. Which not
knowledge is Bondage? Not knowing your own self. Not knowing undifferentiated self.
As we have already explained, there is nothing left separate from Jait prakasha, the conscious self,
nor that exists, nor that is worth existing. So, Malesya apikasata, Mala also does not exist.
So, how can that Mala come in front of you and put obstacles and bondage before you? It
cannot be. So, Vedavadokht prakraya parihairena, what is Mala? He says, Mala, Agjanam is Chanti,
Samsaarankulkar. Mala is not some dirt. Mala is only ignorance. Ignorance of undifferentiated nature.
And knowledge of differentiated nature is Mala. That is Agjana and that is that gives sprout to Samsaar.
That gives sprout to repeated births and deaths. Samsaarankulkar. Samsaar means the wheel of repeated
births and deaths. Agjana, Bidadi, Lokas, Tata, Sreshti, Samrati. By this differentiated knowledge and
undifferentiated knowledge, not knowing. When you know differentiatedly, when you don't know
undifferentiatedly, by this ignorance, Lokas, Bidadi, one gets bondage, one gets bound in the wheel
of repeated births and deaths. And it is why Tata, Sreshti, Samrati, he gets births and deaths in
innumerable way. These two references are of Mali Vijaya and Sarvajara. Mala, Mala,
Magjana, Michanti is the reference of Mali Vijaya and Agjana, Bidadi, Lokas is the reference of Sarvajara,
Tantra. So, by this, Yashankocho Aavasita Parmesharyana, that contraction or limitation or the way of
being shank is shown by Parmeshara. Sasad-Tantra, Aavasita, Sarvapu, Gopana, Rupaya, Mahamaya,
Shakhtya, by which energy, by the energy of his great illusio energy, great power of illusion.
And that power of illusion, which has reason, by his freedom, by the energy of his freedom.
And by the energy of freedom, he tries to conceal his nature. Just for a play, Sarvapu, Gopana,
Rupaya, Sarvapu, Gopana, Rupaya, I mean just to conceal his nature in the way of a play, not in the way
of some depression or for the pleasure. And that contraction or limitation, he reveals where
on which basis, Swatvini, in his own self, the self which is Agashikalpe, which has no vacuum,
it is only vacuum, his self is only vacuum, full of consciousness, vacuum, full of consciousness.
And in that vacuum, which is full of consciousness, this contraction or limitation is shown
from Anastasiva to limited Jeeva, Maya Pramaterintha. And that showing that limitation or contraction
is called Bandha, is called Bandha. Sayeva, Sivadeva, Akya, Tya, Atmakal, Agyana, Subhava,
and that contraction is Agyana, Subhava, not knowledge, not knowing. It is the formation of, not knowing.
Ignorance, of what? Ignorance of oneness of Shiva. Let's see if it was oneness of Shiva. I think
the sound has also come in this. And that bondage is just when you feel yourself incomplete,
you agree that you are incomplete, you are not full. And that is Anamala. And that is Sankochtigya,
that is knowledge, which is shrunk. And ignorance, which is shrunk. Knowledge of what?
Knowledge of differentiated world. Ignorance of what? Ignorance of?
Undifferentiated state. When you don't know, you are undifferentiated state, that is again
when you know that differentiated state, that is also Gyan. That Gyan is bondage and that Agyan is
also bondage. Yathachaya within the Simalasya Anupanatum. So Mala, bondage is not separate from the
being. Bondage is attached with being. So, bondage has not, in other words, come from another
department. It has not, it is your own freedom. It is your own free will that you have put bondage,
you have put bondage in your own nature. It has not come from another agency. So,
Vedereksa Mala is Anupanatum. It is not possible that Mala will come to you from other department.
It has been created by your own freedom. This way I have explained,
came Raja, the commentator of Shiv Sutra says, this way I have explained this in the commentary
of Sachanda in 5th chapter and at the time of the discussion of initiation, Diksha Vichari.
And this I have explained with that here, vividly. This explanation of Sutra is explained in
Spanda Kairika in this Kairika, Neja Shuddha Samaarthachaya. When you become worthless, you become
strengthless, incapable by your own freedom, by your own freedom, by your own freedom,
you become incapable of anything.
It is not only that knowledge is not only bondage. You can know this is also bondage.
Knowledge of Aatmuni, Anatmita-bhumanu, Rupa, Kyaitha-Lakya, Gyan-Aatma-Kham, Gyanam.
A Gyan-Aatma-Kham, Gyanam. When you put knowledge in your nature that I am not self,
I am not real self, I am not universal consciousness. That only is not bondage. Anatmuni, Shri Radha,
when you put ego on your body, that too is also bondage. So, these two ways you get the
explanation of this Sutra, Gyanambandha. So, it comes a Gyanambandha and Gyanambandha.
That first way, Gyanambandha, not knowing your own nature is bondage,
Gyanambandha knowing your body as your own nature is bondage.
This is Anumala. No, both are Anumala in two ways. This is explained in this Kairika,
in Spanda, Paramrata-rasa-apaya, when the supreme nectar is carried away from your nature.
Apaya means being carried away. Aivam, Chaitanya-Shabdya-na-Ukhtam, Yat-Kincheth.
Aivam, Chaitanya-Shabdya-na-Ukhtam, Yat-Kincheth, Swatantra-Atma-Kham-Rupa.
By Chaitanya, we have concluded that Chaitanya means complete freedom,
complete freedom of universal consciousness. In that Saurupa,
Tattra, Chitathmani-apaya, Swatantra-Atma-Vigyana-Kalva,
Upurnam, Manyata, Mahatra-Atma-na-Rupa-na, Swatantra-apaya, Dehada-Avoduru-apaya-na,
Anathmani, Atvantabya, Mahatra-Atma-na-Rupa-na, Deeprakaram, Anumala, and Inusutra-na-Sutra-atma.
So Anumala is defined in this Sutra in two ways. First way is Chitathmani-apaya,
Swatantra-Atma-Vigyana-Kalva. Although you realize the nature of consciousness,
you are always conscious, you are always aware, but Upurnam, Manyata, Mahatra-Atma-na-Rupa-na,
but you feel that this consciousness lives only up to the end of Samadhi.
When Samadhi is over, this consciousness is called consciousness,
the state of consciousness is also over. So this is one way of Anumala.
And another second way of Anumala is Swatantra-apaya, Dehada-Avoduru-apaya-na,
Anathmani-Atmata-Bimana-Atma-na-Rupa-na. If you are free, if you are free,
in coming out from Samadhi, in external world, but in external world you lose the consciousness of
your own nature. You have to return to internal world again. So this is another way of Anumala,
this is also a bondage. Deepakaram, Anum, Anum, Anu, Suthi, Anu, Suthi.
Either you remain always in Samadhi and you are in your own real nature of consciousness.
As soon as you come out from that real nature to the external world, you begin to lose that nature.
So this Anumala pervades in two worlds, in external world and in internal world.
In internal world, it pervades, you cannot come out from that internal world.
In external world, it pervades, as soon as you come out in external world, finished.
The consciousness of your real nature is over. This is explained in the Shloka of Prithmigya-Karika
in this Shloka. So atantreha-haneer, bodhasya, so atantre-sya-pya-bhodata,
dhidana-avam-malamidam, sasurupa-apahaneeta. Sometimes there is no freedom. In consciousness,
in the state of your consciousness, there is no freedom. That consciousness comes off its own
accord, not at your will. The state of conscious being comes by the grace of God, not by your will.
This is Soatantreha-haneer. You have not Soatantreha in that. This is Anumala. This is the
and Soatantre-sya-pya-bhodata. If you find Soatantreha, but you don't find the way you had been experiencing
that universal consciousness. In summary, you don't find in such a way. It is lessened there
in Soatantreha. So this way, this Anumala is said to be twofold. One is Soatantreha-hane,
one is aboda. Sometimes there is no freedom. Sometimes there is no awareness. This way,
sasurupa-apahaneeta. This way, his real nature is carried away from him. Taken away from him.
